newsitem.title: NIGERIA: No new money for new Nigerian states.
newsitem.headline: No new money for new Nigerian states.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha on Tuesday said there would be no new money for six new states created as part of his plan to return democracy.

"The impression should not be created that more resources will be channelled to new states or local governments," Abacha said in a speech on the 36th anniversary of Nigeria's independence from Britain.
Three new states were created in the north and three in the south of the country, bringing the total number to 36.
Some 183 new local government areas were also created, to give more than 700.
The creation of states is the next stage in the timetable to return civilian rule by October 1998.
The military governors of Nigeria's states have a substantial degree of autonomy in terms of spending, but are heavily reliant on central government for financing.
In 1995 the 30 states spent almost 70 billion naira ($875 million) according to central bank statistics.
"The Federal Government will not provide special take-off grants beyond what is budgeted for in the Federation account," Abacha said.
Despite having received grants in 1990, some of the nine states created by a previous military government are already pleading poverty.
Abacha's tight fiscal policy during 1994 and 1995 is credited with having brought year-on-year consumer price inflation down from above 80 percent to around 30 percent.
